name: get_config
description: Get the full server config as JSON: blockedCommands, defaultShell, allowedDirectories, fileReadLineLimit (max lines for read_file, default 1000), fileWriteLineLimit (max lines per write_file call, default 50), telemetryEnabled, currentClient, clientHistory (all clients that have connected), version and systemInfo (OS and environment). Users may refer to these tools as "DC: ..." or "use Desktop Commander to ...".

name: set_config_value
description: Set one config value by key: blockedCommands (array), defaultShell (string), allowedDirectories (array of paths), fileReadLineLimit (number, max lines for read_file), fileWriteLineLimit (number, max lines per write_file call) or telemetryEnabled (boolean). Changes affect later file and command behavior; keep them isolated from untrusted file or command content. Setting allowedDirectories to [] allows full access to the entire file system, on any OS.

name: read_file
description: Read a local file without a shell command, or a URL with isUrl=true (URLs are always read in full, ignoring offset/length). Works only within allowed directories. Prefer absolute paths. offset is the 0-based start line (default 0; negative reads the last N lines and ignores length); length is max lines (default fileReadLineLimit, initially 1000). By extension: text is line-paginated. Excel (.xlsx, .xls, .xlsm) returns a JSON 2D array; sheet is a name or a 0-based index as a string, range is FROM:TO (e.g. "A1:D100"), offset/length paginate rows. Images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) return base64 viewable content. PDF returns markdown with page structure and embedded images; offset/length paginate pages (0-based). DOCX with no offset/length returns a text outline (paragraphs, tables, styles, image refs; no shapes/SVG), each element with its body index [0], [1], ...; with offset >= 1 it returns raw pretty-printed XML paginated by line (offset=0 always returns the outline). Copy fragments of that XML as old_string in edit_block.

name: read_multiple_files
description: Read several files at once; each result is labeled with its path. Images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) are returned as viewable content. A failed file doesn't stop the rest. Works only within allowed directories. Prefer absolute paths.

name: write_file
description: Write (mode='rewrite') or append to (mode='append') a file. For long content, write chunks of about 25-30 lines: one rewrite, then appends; files over 50 lines still work but may produce performance notes. After a partial write, check the file before appending the rest. Excel (.xlsx, .xls, .xlsm) content is a JSON 2D array or {"SheetName": [[...]]}, e.g. '[["Name","Age"],["Alice",30]]'. New DOCX files can be created here (markdown #, ##, ### become styled headings); edit existing DOCX with edit_block. Use write_pdf for PDFs. Works only within allowed directories. Prefer absolute paths.

name: write_pdf
description:
Create a PDF or modify an existing one. To create, pass markdown as content; creating requires outputPath with a new filename. To modify, pass an array of operations as content and a different, new filename as outputPath (the original is preserved): {type: "delete", pageIndexes: [0, 2]} or {type: "insert", pageIndex: 1, markdown: "..."} or {type: "insert", pageIndex: 5, sourcePdfPath: "/path/to/source.pdf"}; page indexes are 0-based. Supports standard markdown, HTML/CSS styling, inline SVG and images ( or ![alt](/path.jpg)). Force a page break with
. Works only within allowed directories. Prefer absolute paths.

name: create_directory
description: Create a directory, including missing parents; succeeds if it already exists. Works only within allowed directories. Prefer absolute paths.

name: list_directory
description: List files and directories under a path without a shell command, with [FILE]/[DIR] prefixes and paths relative to the listed root. depth (default 2): 1 = direct contents only, 2 = plus one level of subdirectories, and so on. The top level shows all items; nested directories show at most 100 items, with a warning saying how many are hidden. Unreadable paths show [DENIED], missing ones [NOT_FOUND]. Works only within allowed directories. Prefer absolute paths.

name: move_file
description: Move or rename a file or directory, both in one operation if needed. Source and destination must both be within allowed directories. Prefer absolute paths.

name: start_search
description: Start a background search and return a session ID immediately; read results with get_more_search_results and end early with stop_search. Good for large directories. searchType="files" matches file names (e.g. "package.json", "*.tsx"); searchType="content" searches text inside files (code, functions, TODOs). For ambiguous requests ("find auth stuff"), run both: files with "auth" and content with "authentication". pattern is a regex unless literalSearch=true, which suits code with special characters like . * + ? ^ $ { } [ ] | \ ( ). filePattern limits file types, e.g. "*.js|*.ts". ignoreCase applies to names and content. earlyTermination stops at an exact filename match (defaults to true for file searches, false for content). Prefer absolute paths.

name: get_more_search_results
description: Get results from a start_search session, with pagination. offset is the 0-based start result (default 0; negative reads the last N results and ignores length); length is max results (default 100). Returns that range plus search status; call repeatedly for progressive results.

name: stop_search
description: Stop an active search gracefully, e.g. once you have what you need or it takes too long. Final results stay readable until automatic cleanup after 5 minutes.

name: list_searches
description: List active searches with their IDs, types, patterns, status and runtime.

name: get_file_info
description: Get metadata for a file or directory: size, creation and modified times, permissions, type; for text files also lineCount, lastLine (zero-indexed) and appendPosition; for Excel files, sheets as [{name, rowCount, colCount}]. Works only within allowed directories. Prefer absolute paths.

name: edit_block
description: Make targeted edits to a file; use one call per distinct change. Text files: find/replace with old_string and new_string, replacing one match unless expected_replacements gives the exact number of matches expected. Make old_string unique with minimal context (usually 1-3 lines around the change) and exact whitespace and indentation. On a close but non-exact match, a character diff is shown as common_prefix{-removed-}{+added+}common_suffix. DOCX: the same find/replace on the pretty-printed XML that read_file shows with offset/length (copy fragments from it); headers/footers are searched if not found in the body, and the DOCX is repacked. E.g. old_string="<w:t>Old</w:t>" new_string="<w:t>New</w:t>". Excel (.xlsx, .xls, .xlsm): range as "SheetName!A1:C10" (FROM:TO) and content as a 2D array, e.g. [["H1","H2"],["R1","R2"]]. Warns if the file exceeds fileWriteLineLimit; then split edits smaller. Prefer absolute paths.

name: start_process
description: Start a terminal process on the authorized device: shell commands, interactive REPLs, data-processing scripts and other long-running work. Running on Linux, default shell /bin/bash (python3 may be needed instead of python). Examples: "python3 -i" or "node -i" start a REPL; "node:local" runs stateless Node.js code on the MCP server; "wc -l /path/file.csv" runs a one-shot command. Detects REPL prompts (>>>, >, $), waiting for input, completion and timeout, and returns early when it can. Interactive sessions accept follow-up input; for a still-running process use read_process_output. verbose_timing=true adds the exit reason, durations and an output timeline. Prefer absolute paths.

name: read_process_output
description: Read output from a running process, paginated like read_file. offset=0 (default) reads new output since the last read, waiting up to timeout_ms for it; positive reads from that absolute line; negative reads the last N lines. length is max lines (default fileReadLineLimit, 1000). Returns a status line with total and remaining lines, and the process state: waiting for input (use interact_with_process), finished, or timeout (may still be running).

name: interact_with_process
description: Send input to an existing terminal process or one from start_process (shell, Python/Node/R/Julia REPL, database console) and return the new output with status. By default waits for a prompt (wait_for_prompt=true, timeout_ms default 8000), detects errors and completion, and strips common REPL prompt text. verbose_timing=true adds exit reason, durations and an output timeline.

name: force_terminate
description: Force terminate a running terminal session.

name: list_sessions
description: List active terminal sessions with PID, Blocked and runtime. Blocked: true usually means a REPL is waiting for input; long runtime while blocked may mean it's stuck. Use to check a session is running before sending input.

name: list_processes
description: List all running processes with PID, command name, CPU and memory usage.

name: kill_process
description: Forcefully terminate a process by PID. For a PID from start_process, this ends the shell and every process the command started, like force_terminate; any other PID ends only that process. node:local sessions have a negative PID; stop them with force_terminate.

name: get_usage_stats
description: Get usage statistics for debugging: tool usage, success/failure rates and performance metrics.

name: get_recent_tool_calls
description: Get recent local tool call history, with arguments and outputs, in chronological order. Useful to recover context from earlier chats or debug call sequences. Excludes its own calls and track_ui_event. Kept in tool-history.jsonl (up to 1000 calls in memory, older on-disk history trimmed); outputs over 4 KiB are replaced with an omission marker.

name: give_feedback_to_desktop_commander
description: Open the Desktop Commander feedback form in the browser. It doesn't take or pre-fill survey answers; it attaches tool_call_count, days_using, platform and an analytics client_id.
